entries.notes: CS in alto slightly altered; tenor free part with leaping figure used in episodes
CS in soprano; bars 5-9 interchanged at the fifteenth
CS in bass in original relationship
CS in soprano interchanging 5-9 at twelfth; tenor continuous semiquavers
CS in alto a third higher (interchanged at tenth then octave)
soprano chief voice after two bars' silence; alternatively alto leads with soprano adding sixths
CS alto doubled by soprano in thirds
solitary note after much four-part writing; CS alto interchanging 5-6 at twelfth
'as if in stretto'; CS in bass with added tenths from alto; ending altered

episodes.name: episode 1
episodes.material: two-part imitation of leaping figure of bar 9 with main CS figure in bass

episodes.name: episode 2
episodes.material: bass repeats leaping figure; tenor and soprano imitate main CS figure

episodes.name: episode 3
episodes.sequence: free rising sequence to perfect cadence in iv at 45

episodes.name: episode 5
episodes.material: altered end of subject imitates falling passage of CS

episodes.name: episode 6
episodes.material: altered subject ending lets tenor imitate CS falling passage

extensions.to: altered ending to perfect cadence at 75

countersubjects.interchange: interchangeable with subject/answer at tenth, twelfth and fifteenth, hence subject or CS can be doubled in thirds or sixths

subject.answer: tonal (subject begins on dominant, answer on tonic); real answer used at 28

claims.claim: Countersubject is interchangeable at the tenth, twelfth and fifteenth, making doubling in thirds/sixths possible
At 32 the CS is a third higher than its original relation: interchanged at tenth then octave
Bar 51 soprano with added sixths could alternatively be heard as alto subject in iv with soprano adding sixths
Final soprano entry at 69 enters 'as if in stretto'
Coda includes a final transformed entry of the subject in the bass
